Evidence-linked critique

Where confidence breaks

Not user research

These are heuristic design observations—not validated Verizon customer findings.

Primary gap

The journey helps customers choose a device, but does not provide one complete, editable view of financial impact before commitment.

1

Costs are distributed across the journey.

2

Trade-in conditions are not integrated into the connected path.

3

The clearest order summary arrives after submission.

Implementation annotations

Behavior that must survive the move to Figma—and into code.

11accessibility requirements mapped
A11Y-001

Structure and order

Every amount remains attached to its label, timing and status in the accessibility tree and responsive reading order.

A11Y-003

Predictable focus

Background recalculation never moves focus. Navigation moves focus to the new screen heading; edits return to the changed section.

A11Y-004

Keyboard complete

Selection, expansion, editing and commitment work without dragging, hover or pointer-only gestures.

A11Y-006

Meaningful updates

Concise live-region messages announce important changes without repeating the complete financial summary.

A11Y-007

Reflow

At 320 CSS pixels, content retains a single meaningful order with no clipped values or horizontal scrolling.

A11Y-009

Safe commitment

Only “Place upgrade order” commits. Repeat submission stays disabled until the result is known.

Figma transfer checklist

Rebuild in this order

  1. 01
    Create pages

    Cover, Flow + IA, Foundations, Components, Desktop flow, Mobile + states, Annotations.

  2. 02
    Create variables

    Color, spacing, radius and type styles from Foundations.

  3. 03
    Create components

    Actions, cards, status tags, progress and Upgrade Impact with documented variants.

  4. 04
    Assemble six screens

    Reuse components; preserve the same content and financial hierarchy.

  5. 05
    Connect prototype

    Happy path, edit loops, mobile summary and representative recovery states.
